title: Laboratory Contamination Prevention

references.label: Biosafety in Microbiological and Biomedical Laboratories (BMBL)

summary: Practices that reduce the likelihood of unwanted organisms entering cultures, reagents, or samples during routine work.
explanation: Prevention rests mainly on consistent aseptic technique, proper media/reagent storage, regular equipment maintenance/cleaning (e.g. incubators, water baths), and prompt investigation of unexpected results that might indicate contamination rather than a true biological finding.
keyPractices: Apply consistent aseptic technique at every transfer step.
Store media and reagents properly and check for signs of contamination (cloudiness, unexpected color change) before use.
Regularly clean and maintain shared equipment (incubators, water baths, refrigerators).
Investigate unexpected results as possible contamination before concluding a novel biological finding.
